statement: Deposits are shallow, almost horizontal, tabular, low-grade bodies in sandstones, quartzites and the Woocalla Dolomite; main ore horizon in gritty sandstones at the unconformity
quote_ocr: The copper deposits comprise shallow, almost horizontal, more or less tabular bodies of generally low grade that occur in sandstones, quartzites and in the Woocalla Dolomite Member. ... The main known ore horizon is confined to red and white gritty sandstones adjacent to the unconformity and, patchily, in dolomite.
author_source: Johns, R.K. 1968. Geology and mineral resources of the Andamooka-Torrens area. Bull. geol. Surv. S. Aust. 41

statement: Copper along the unconformity between Pernatty Grit (Pandurra) and a younger sandstone next to a collenia reef; the early Marinoan shoreline controlled deposition
quote_ocr: At Mount Gunson, copper deposits occur along an unconformable surface between dense Pernatty Grit and a younger sandstone adjacent to what is considered to be a collenia reef. ... the early Marinoan shoreline provided a sedimentary control on copper deposition.
author_source: Johns, R.K. 1968. Geology and mineral resources of the Andamooka-Torrens area. Bull. geol. Surv. S. Aust. 41

statement: WWII open-cut production 32,380 tons at 3.5% Cu; King (1950) expected 150,000 tons of 3% Cu from known exposures
quote_ocr: during the period 1941-1943 some 32,380 tons of ore averaging 3.5 per cent Cu were mined ... King (1950) concluded that 150,000 tons of 3 per cent Cu might be expected from the known exposures in this locality.
author_source: Johns, R.K. 1968. Geology and mineral resources of the Andamooka-Torrens area. Bull. geol. Surv. S. Aust. 41

statement: Ore up to 14 ft (4.3 m) thick; orebodies elongated east-west, at two levels; Gunyah workings over 2,500 ft by 60-300 ft on the lagoon floor
quote_ocr: The orebodies ... appear to occupy two distinct levels ... They are elongated in an east-west direction. ... over a thickness of up to 14ft. with grades up to 9 per cent Cu ... The workings extend over an elongate area 2,500ft. x 60ft. to 300ft. on the lagoon floor
author_source: Johns, R.K. 1968. Geology and mineral resources of the Andamooka-Torrens area. Bull. geol. Surv. S. Aust. 41

statement: Deposits localised within or adjacent to one bed of dolomitic limestone (Woocalla); its limits define the area beyond which ore is extremely unlikely; typically 'red bed' occurrences
quote_ocr: The mineral deposits were found to be localized within or adjacent to a distinctive bed of dolomitic limestone. ... its limits fairly well define the area beyond which the chances for ore are extremely unlikely. ... The copper deposits are typically "Red Bed" occurrences.
author_source: RB 18/00119 (Assistant Government Geologist; published as Dickinson 1942, Bull. 20 pp. 50-65)

statement: Gustafsen possible tonnage 395,000 tons at 3.14% Cu; reserves about 18,000 tons at 4%+
quote_ocr: Gustafsen made a possible tonnage estimate of 395,000 tons at 3.14%. ... Ore reserves stand at roughly 18,000 tons

statement: Copper deposited syngenetically with the lithic (disconformity) sandstone; the lithic sandstone is visible or inferred in all areas of known mineralisation
quote_ocr: Available evidence suggests that the copper mineralization was deposited syngenetically with the lithic sandstone. ... In all areas of known mineralization the lithic sandstone is either visible or inferred.
author_source: Austminex, SML 96/121 annual report and Geology of the Pernatty Lagoon area (Env 00674)

statement: Marinoan lutites are red-brown with green laminae; copper occurs in green shale phases, not all green shales cupriferous
quote_ocr: These lutites are red-brown shales and siltstones with green shale laminae ... in green shale phases of the lutite, although not all green shales are cupriferous
author_source: Thomson, B.P. RB 60/00004 (Source and distribution of heavy metals in Cambrian and Marinoan shelf sediments)

statement: The Pandurra-Whyalla disconformity 90 miles south (Pandurra prospect) is the surface considered to control copper at Mount Gunson-Pernatty Lagoon
unit: km (90 miles, Pandurra prospect to Mount Gunson)
quote_ocr: The surface of disconformity with the underlying Pandurra Formation is observable some six miles to the south of Pandurra H.S. This surface is considered to be that which acted as a stratigraphic control in copper mineralisation in the Mt. Gunson-Pernatty Lagoon locality some 90 miles to the north.
author_source: Mason, M.G. RB 65/00068 (Copper prospect, Pandurra, preliminary report)
note: text layer; copper at the same level as Mount Gunson

statement: Ore confined to the Pandurra 'window' close to reef-dolomite facies of the Woocalla; elsewhere the Woocalla is black dolomitic shale; ore in depressions of the pre-Woocalla surface
quote_ocr: known economic concentrations of copper ... are restricted ... to the eastern and southern boundaries, close to the Woocalla Dolomite, where this horizon is represented by a dolomite or dolomitic limestone of possible stromatolite reef origin. Elsewhere, the Woocalla Formation ... [is] a black dolomitic shale and not reef-like carbonate ... Localisation of copper ores has a further control ... in depressions in the pre-Woocalla erosion surface on the Pandurra Formation.
author_source: Tonkin, D.G. PMR 149/71, Mt Gunson ore controls as a basis for further exploration (Env 01563)

statement: Three million tons of 1% Cu mineralisation in the Gunson area; source argued as syngenetic Cu (300-500 ppm) in the Woocalla dolomite
quote_ocr: Copper values of 300 to 500 p.p.m. have been recorded in unmineralised dolomite in areas near copper workings. ... Three million tons of 1% Cu Mineralization in the Gunson area
author_source: Tonkin, D.G. PMR 149/71

statement: Woocalla Dolomite and its deep-water black shaly siltstone traced from under Mount Gunson, under Oakden Hills, to south of Monalena, and identified in Woomera No. 1 at 308-454.5 m
quote_ocr: The Woocalla Dolomite and its deep water equivalent, a black shaley siltstone, has now been traced southward from under Mount Gunson, under the Oakden Hills, to south of Monalena ... It has been further identified from the Woomera No. 1 Bore as being present below Woomera township at a depth of 308 metres to 454.5 metres.
author_source: Pacminex, EL 81 progress report to 19/10/1973 (Env 02330)
note: belt length computed in the notebook from bore coordinates

statement: Black-shale facies fills broad basins around the Oakden Hills Pandurra ridges; the black-shale basin extends west to Lake MacFarlane
quote_ocr: To the north, west and south of the ridge complex, the post-Pandurra surface slopes away into broad basins of deposition, infilled with the black shale facies of the Woocalla Dolomite. A scout drilling programme between Oakden Hills and Lake MacFarlane has shown that the black shale basin extends westward to Lake MacFarlane.
author_source: Maiden, K.J. PMR 97/73, Oakden Hills-Lake MacFarlane (Env 02330)

statement: Maximum unit thicknesses, Oakden Hills-Lake MacFarlane: Woocalla 130 m, Whyalla 100 m, Tregolana 140 m, Pandurra >100 m
quote_ocr: Woocalla Dolomite 130 m ... Whyalla Sandstone 100 m ... Tregolana Shale 140 m ... Pandurra Formation >100 m
author_source: Maiden, K.J. PMR 97/73

statement: Facies of the Woocalla: black shale (deeper water), dolomitic shale, laminated, oolitic, stromatolitic dolomite, dolomitic mud and silt (supratidal), red and green shale; the deeper-water, lagoon and supratidal facies may carry reducing conditions
quote_ocr: Of these facies types, those deposited in deeper water, in shallow lagoons and in the supratidal zone may be associated with reducing conditions favourable for the precipitation of sulphides.
author_source: Maiden, K.J. PMR 58/74, Facies variations in the Woocalla Formation (Env 06611)

statement: West of the Pernatty Culmination the shoreline fringe of dolomite is generally less than 500 m wide before grading through dolomitic shale into black shale
quote_ocr: In the Mt. Gunson, McLeay and Oakden Hills area, the shoreline fringe of dolomite is generally less than 500 m in width before grading through dolomitic shale into black shale.
author_source: Maiden, K.J. PMR 58/74

statement: Black shale 120 m thick in the Woomera Bore; unit up to 130 m
quote_ocr: In the Woomera Bore, the unit consists of 120 m of black shale. ... The thickness of the unit (up to 130 m)
author_source: Maiden, K.J. PMR 58/74

statement: Between 'Pandurra' and 'Hesso' the black shale changes shoreward into red and green shale filling a broad channel: detrital deposition in an oxygenated environment
quote_ocr: Between "Pandurra" and "Hesso", the black shale changes shoreward into red and green shale. Cross sections show that this facies occupies a broad channel at the western edge of the Woocalla Basin ... This facies indicates a change to detrital deposition in an oxygenated environment as opposed to the reducing environment of the black shale facies.
author_source: Maiden, K.J. PMR 58/74

statement: Black shale cored in 6 holes about 10 km apart (Lake Dutton, Noranda): minor sulphide and above-normal metals in every hole
quote_ocr: Subsequently, the black shale was cored in 6 drill holes spaced about 10 km apart. Minor amounts of sulphide and above normal metal values were detected in every hole.
author_source: Maiden, K.J. PMR 58/74
note: reduced facies present at every sampled site over a ~50 km spread

statement: Cu highest near the basin edge and falling over 15 km (4,600 ppm at 1 km to 180 ppm at 15 km); Pb-Zn peaks further out (Zn 9,200 ppm at 8 km)
unit: km (Cu decay length scale, basin edge to LD4)
quote_ocr: Higher copper values occur towards the edge of the basin of deposition, Pb-Zn values further away from the edge ... LD1 1 km 4600 1600 2200 ... LD3 8 km 400 3000 9200 LD4 15 km 180 800 3000
author_source: Maiden, K.J. PMR 58/74

statement: North of the Cattlegrid Cu 5,700-6,500 ppm in dolomitic shale 0.25-0.75 km from the palaeo-shoreline, black shale at 1.25 km 2,400 ppm Cu and Pb
quote_ocr: MG21 0.25 Dolomitic Shale 5700 130 820 MG17 0.75 Dolomitic Shale 6500 340 890 MG18 1.25 Black Shale 2400 2400 1100
author_source: Maiden, K.J. PMR 58/74

statement: Sweet Nell: 213,000 tonnes of 1.22% Cu in a 1-2 m shale on the post-Pandurra surface; Gully 0.1-0.4% Cu over almost 1 km2; Pb-Zn zones 6-9 m thick over 1.5 and 2.5 km2
quote_ocr: Copper mineralisation at the Sweet Nell Mine occurs in a shale bed, approximately 1-2 m thick, underlying dolomite. The shale lies directly on the post-Pandurra palaeo-surface. ... an estimated 213,000 tonnes of 1.22% Cu. ... Gully area - values in the range 0.1 - 0.4% Cu over an area of almost 1 km2 ... The zones are both 6-9 m thick.
author_source: Maiden, K.J. PMR 58/74
note: OCR areas '2.5 km' and '1.5 km' read as km2

statement: Controls: facies (dolomitic mud and silt; dolomitic shale with Cu inshore and Pb-Zn offshore), a rapid oxidising-to-reducing change, and depressions in the post-Pandurra palaeo-surface; compared with the Copperbelt, White Pine and Kupferschiefer
quote_ocr: the actual controlling factor may be a rapid change from oxidising to reducing conditions ... higher metal concentrations appear to be associated with local depressions (basins or channels) in the post-Pandurra palaeo-surface. ... The Woocalla Dolomite has been compared to the Kupferschiefer ... by Dunlop and Dunlop (1970), and to the Zambian Copperbelt by Johns (1972).
author_source: Maiden, K.J. PMR 58/74

statement: INPUT airborne EM may be picking up depressions in the post-Pandurra surface; MG14 target found by INPUT, weak EM and good IP over it
quote_ocr: The INPUT method is possibly picking up depressions in the post-Pandurra palaeo-surface. ... Follow-up geophysics in the MG14 area produced a weak E.M. cross-over and a quite good I.P. anomaly coinciding with the INPUT anomaly.
author_source: Maiden, K.J. PMR 58/74

statement: The Sturtian disconformity is a locus for copper at the base of the Woocalla; the Marinoan transgression is the locus for Mount Gunson stratiform copper in the Whyalla Sandstone
quote_ocr: The Sturtian disconformity is a locus for later copper mineralisation at the base of the Woocalla Dolomite ... This Marinoan transgression is a locus for the Mount Gunson stratiform copper mineralisation in the Whyalla Sandstone Member.
author_source: Thomson, B.P., Forbes, B.G. and Coats, R.P. RB 74/00135 (for Knight ed.)

statement: Discrete, shallow, more or less tabular low-grade bodies up to 5 m thick along the unconformities separating Whyalla Sandstone and Woocalla Dolomite from the Pandurra; open-cut reserves 3 Mt of +1% Cu (1970)
quote_ocr: The known copper deposits comprise discrete, shallow, more or less tabular bodies of generally low grade that range up to 5 m in thickness and are concentrated along unconformities which separate the Whyalla Sandstone and Woocalla Dolomite from the underlying Pandurra Formation. ... open-cut reserves were reported to total three million tonnes of +1% copper ore.
author_source: Johns, R.K. RB 74/00197 (Adelaide Geosyncline and Stuart Shelf, sundry mineralisation)
note: catalogue year 1975 is the book; the report is dated 9 Oct 1974

statement: Pyroxene basalts of presumed Willouran age, over 200 m thick, under a Pandurra of at least 200 m; Woocalla up to 150 m
quote_ocr: Pyroxene basalts of presumed Willouran age and exceeding 200 m in thickness are succeeded by the Pandurra Formation, a clastic sequence of horizontally disposed quartzites at least 200 m in thickness ... The dolomite which ranges up to 150 m in thickness
author_source: Johns, R.K. RB 74/00197
note: bears on Level 2 (basalt below the Pandurra at the analog)

statement: Zinc and lead proven over a wide area in dolomitic black shales, zones up to 10 m thick at 0.2% Pb and 0.3% Zn; localisation governed by the Pernatty Culmination and the unconformities separating reef dolomite, black shale and sandstones
quote_ocr: Zinc and lead, in subeconomic concentrations, have been proven by drilling to occur over a wide area in dolomitic black shales. ... Several zones ranging up to 10 m in thickness have been proven to contain 0.2% lead and 0.3% zinc ... the proximity of the Pernatty Culmination ... and the unconformities separating reef dolomite, a black shale facies and sandstones
author_source: Johns, R.K. RB 74/00197

statement: Cattle Grid ore mainly in the brecciated weathered top of the Pandurra; mineralisation crosses a valley and ridges; an MG14 basic dyke is proposed as the metal source
quote_ocr: The ore zone of the Cattle Grid is principally the brecciated zone created during the weathering of the Pandurra Formation. ... the Cattle Grid mineralisation does not appear to have been significantly influenced by the Pandurra Topography ... the possible importance of this basic igneous activity directly related to copper mineralisation at Mount Gunson
author_source: Pacminex, text signed 3/3/1975, filed under Tonkin PMR 140/76 (July 1976) (Env 06593)
note: cross-check only until its circulation date is settled

statement: Copper in sandstone and dolomite adjacent to a stromatolite reef about a basement high (Pernatty Culmination); widespread low-grade Zn-Pb-Cu sulphide in laterally equivalent dolomitic black shales in restricted lagoonal depressions of the Pandurra surface
quote_ocr: Copper mineralisation appears to be concentrated in sandstone and dolomite adjacent to and within a stromatolite reef complex about a basement high (the Pernatty culmination) whereas zinc and lead, in subeconomic concentrations, occur in laterally equivalent dolomitic black shales which accumulated in a restricted lagoonal environment, in depressions within the Pandurra Formation.
author_source: Johns, R.K. RB 72/00189 (Base metal mineralisation in the Pernatty Lagoon region)

statement: Copper deposits are tabular bodies up to 15 ft (4.6 m) thick along the disconformities; open-cut reserves 3.2 million tons at the May 1970 reopening
unit: tons (open-cut reserve, grade not stated here)
quote_ocr: The known copper deposits comprise discrete, shallow, gently undulating more or less tabular bodies of generally low grade that range up to 15ft. in thickness ... open-cut reserves were put at 3.2 million tons of copper ore.
author_source: Johns, R.K. RB 72/00189 (Base metal mineralisation in the Pernatty Lagoon region)

statement: Dolomitic black shales (Woocalla) intersected over a wide area in water bores: Woomera No. 1 372 ft of dark-grey laminated shale (1,118-1,490 ft), Beda bore 14 ft, a bore 4 miles north of Maslin over 100 ft; absent at Yudnapinna and Lake MacFarlane; black shales at the Pandurra prospect are lateral equivalents
quote_ocr: Dolomitic black shales have been intersected in drilling for water supplies over a wide area. Woomera No. 1 bore passed through 372ft. of dark-grey finely laminated shale and dolomitic shale between 1 118ft. and 1 490ft. In Beda bore 14ft. of this formation were intersected ... However, the formation appears to be absent in the Yudnapinna H.S. area and at Lake MacFarlane. ... Black shales exposed at the copper prospect, 2 miles south-east of Pandurra H.S. are lateral equivalents.
author_source: Johns, R.K. RB 72/00189 (Base metal mineralisation in the Pernatty Lagoon region)
note: Maiden (Sep 1973) later reports black shale reaching Lake MacFarlane; the two disagree

statement: 1971 Noranda/SADM programme: 7 widely spaced holes from Oakden Hills to beyond Lake Dutton; 6 intersected Woocalla black or dolomitic shale (12 to 129 m), LD7 found Whyalla Sandstone directly on Pandurra
quote_ocr: Seven widely spaced holes were subsequently drilled in a region of sparse outcrop extending from Oakden Hills H.S. to beyond Lake Dutton. ... LD7 ... was drilled to completion without encountering shale. The Whyalla Sandstone 120ft. in thickness, rests directly on the Pandurra Formation.
author_source: Johns, R.K. RB 72/00189 (Base metal mineralisation in the Pernatty Lagoon region)
note: same LD holes as Maiden 1974 'six holes about 10 km apart'; counted once; thicknesses in mount_gunson_LD_holes_1971.csv

statement: 1968 Winnie Pinnie drilling (30 holes at about half-mile spacing): Woocalla more or less mineralised throughout, filling depressions, up to 130 ft; Pb-Zn highest in two northerly troughs about 1 x 0.5 mile and 2 x 0.5 mile; shales over the highs more dolomitic and poorer
quote_ocr: The underlying Woocalla Dolomite proved to be more or less mineralised throughout ... Base metal contents proved to be highest in two concealed sub-parallel shallow troughs ... the westernmost zone is almost one mile long and one half mile wide ... another zone almost two miles long and one half mile wide ... the shales over the more elevated portions of this surface were more dolomitic and relatively deficient in base metals
author_source: Johns, R.K. RB 72/00189 (Base metal mineralisation in the Pernatty Lagoon region)

statement: Mineralised black shale in a basement trough over 20 miles (32 km) between Winnie Pinnie and Greenfields Dam; area of interest a corridor about 6 miles (10 km) wide trending north from Winnie Pinnie to Birthday siding
quote_ocr: this interpretation narrows down the general area of interest to a corridor some six miles in width trending slightly east of north, from south of the Winnie Pinnie Dam area to Birthday siding. ... black shale in a basement trough extending over a distance of 20 miles between Winnie Pinnie and Greenfields Dam
author_source: Johns, R.K. RB 72/00189 (Base metal mineralisation in the Pernatty Lagoon region)

statement: East Lagoon orebody (April 1970): measured 203,000 short tons at 1.43% Cu, indicated 46,000 at 1.26%, inferred 26,000 at 1.05%; mineralisation averages 11.5 ft (3.5 m) thick, most ore within the red quartzite (Pandurra), trends still open
quote_ocr: Measured Ore 203,000 1.43 Indicated Ore 46,000 1.26 Inferred Ore 26,000 1.05 ... The average thickness of mineralisation (11.5') is thin and can be effectively mined in one level. ... They also show how most of the ore occurs within the red quartzite. ... Mineralisation trends on the west, east, and northeast sides are still open
author_source: Mathias, W.F. Evaluation of the East Lagoon orebody (Env 06604)

statement: Controls: the Pernatty Culmination (a basement high with an algal reef, intruded by a swarm of basic dykes), the Pandurra/Woocalla/Whyalla disconformities, dolomite as a pH trap, basement fractures; dolerite near Katunga Hills carries about 500 ppm Cu; analogies with the Kupferschiefer and the Rhodesian copper belt
quote_ocr: The Pernatty Culmination, underlain by basement rocks which are intruded by a swarm of basic dykes and dislocated by a system of major fractures, comprise a potential zone of weakness through which mineralising solutions could have migrated. ... Three holes ... intersected dolerite averaging almost 500 ppm copper ... Analogies may be drawn between the mineralised black shales (Woocalla Dolomite) and the Kupferschiefer of northern Europe while the association ... flanking collenia reefs on basement highs invites comparison with deposits of the Rhodesian copper belt
author_source: Johns, R.K. RB 72/00189 (Base metal mineralisation in the Pernatty Lagoon region)
note: ties the Level 2 basalt/dolerite source to the Level 3 reduced trap at the analog
